# pbs_realm_openid (Resource)

Manages an OpenID Connect realm of a Proxmox Backup Server: users sign in to PBS through an identity provider such as Authentik, Keycloak or Microsoft Entra ID. PBS knows them as `<name>@<realm>`, the name being the value of `username_claim`. Only users that exist can sign in — create them with `pbs_user`, or let PBS create them at their first sign-in with `autocreate` — and they have no privileges until a `pbs_acl` grants them some.

PBS contacts nothing when it saves a realm: a wrong issuer URL, client ID or client key shows only when someone signs in. The identity provider must accept PBS's address, such as `https://pbs.example.com:8007`, as a redirect URI.

**The client key** of a confidential client goes either in `client_key`, which Terraform stores in state, as sensitive — PBS returns it, so a change made outside Terraform shows in the plan — or in `client_key_wo` with `client_key_wo_version`, which keep it out of the plan and state. A realm created with neither is a public client, which signs in without a key. Moving from one to the other sends the key once. Removing `client_key` deletes the key from PBS; removing `client_key_wo`, or leaving both out after an import, keeps the key PBS has. An import reads neither: a configuration with a key sends it in the next apply.

~> **Only one realm is the default.** `default = true` takes the flag from the realm that had it, the built-in `pam` and `pbs` and realms outside Terraform included. Set it on one realm only: two realms with `default = true` take it from each other on every apply.

Changing `realm` or `username_claim` replaces the realm, which creates it with what the configuration holds: a key left to PBS — after an import, or after removing `client_key_wo` — is lost then, and the plan warns. PBS keeps the users of a deleted realm, and their ACL entries; after a new `username_claim`, users sign in under the names it gives, and users made for the old one no longer match.

Managing realms needs `Realm.Allocate` on `/access/domains`; reading one `Sys.Audit` there.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Sign-in through Authentik. In Authentik, PBS is an OAuth2/OpenID provider
# with an application whose slug, here "pbs", ends the issuer URL; its
# redirect URI is the address of PBS's web interface, such as
# https://pbs.example.com:8007. PBS contacts Authentik only when someone signs
# in, so a wrong issuer or key shows then, not on apply.
resource "pbs_realm_openid" "authentik" {
  realm      = "authentik"
  issuer_url = "https://authentik.example.com/application/o/pbs/"
  client_id  = "pbs"
  comment    = "Authentik"

  # The client secret is write-only: it never reaches the plan or state, and
  # PBS receives it when the realm is created and whenever
  # client_key_wo_version changes. client_key would keep it in state instead,
  # where a change made outside Terraform shows.
  client_key_wo         = var.authentik_client_secret
  client_key_wo_version = 1

  # Users are <Authentik username>@authentik. Changing the claim later
  # replaces the realm.
  username_claim = "preferred_username"

  # Users that do not exist yet are created at their first sign-in, without
  # privileges; the sign-in form preselects the realm.
  autocreate = true
  default    = true
}

# A user of the realm, with read access to the datastores' contents. Created
# beforehand, it can sign in with autocreate = false too.
resource "pbs_user" "alice" {
  userid = "alice@${pbs_realm_openid.authentik.realm}"
  email  = "alice@example.com"
}

resource "pbs_acl" "alice" {
  path    = "/datastore"
  auth_id = pbs_user.alice.userid
  role    = "DatastoreReader"
}

variable "authentik_client_secret" {
  description = "Client secret of the PBS provider in Authentik."
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
  ephemeral   = true
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `client_id` (String) Client ID of PBS at the identity provider.
- `issuer_url` (String) Issuer of the identity provider, exactly as `issuer` in its discovery document, `<issuer_url>/.well-known/openid-configuration`, has it — for Authentik `https://authentik.example.com/application/o/<application slug>/`, trailing slash included. An `https://` or, for tests, `http://` URL without credentials, query or fragment.
- `realm` (String) Realm name, 2 to 32 characters: letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, not starting with `.` or `-`, and neither `pam` nor `pbs`, the built-in realms. Users of the realm are `<name>@<realm>`. Changing it replaces the realm.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `acr_values` (List of String) Authentication context class references PBS asks the identity provider for, in order of preference; which it honours is up to the provider. None when left out.
- `audiences` (Set of String) Audiences PBS accepts in ID tokens besides `client_id`, for identity providers whose tokens name more than one. When left out, PBS refuses ID tokens with an audience other than `client_id`. Each is up to 256 characters. Needs PBS 4.2.1 or newer.
- `autocreate` (Boolean) Whether PBS creates a user who signs in for the first time, with the email address and names from their claims, and no privileges. Defaults to `false`: only users that exist can sign in.
- `client_key` (String, Sensitive) Client secret of a confidential client, which Terraform stores in state, as sensitive. PBS returns it, so a change made outside Terraform shows in the plan. Removing it deletes the key from PBS, which then signs in as a public client. Conflicts with `client_key_wo`.
- `client_key_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Client secret of a confidential client, instead of `client_key`, with which it conflicts. Write-only: Terraform passes it to PBS without storing it in the plan or state. PBS does return it, but the provider leaves it out of state, so a change made outside Terraform goes unnoticed. PBS receives it when the realm is created and whenever `client_key_wo_version` changes; removing both leaves the key PBS has. Requires `client_key_wo_version`, and Terraform or OpenTofu 1.11 or later.
- `client_key_wo_version` (Number) Version of `client_key_wo`, which Terraform stores in its place. Change it — increment it, say — to send a new `client_key_wo`; removing it, with `client_key_wo`, leaves the value on the server as it is. Requires `client_key_wo`.
- `comment` (String) Free-form comment, up to 128 characters on one line.
- `default` (Boolean) Whether the sign-in form preselects this realm. Only one realm is the default: `true` takes the flag from the realm that had it. Defaults to `false`.
- `prompt` (String) OpenID `prompt` PBS sends to the identity provider: `login` or `consent` to have it ask the user again, `select_account` to let them choose an account, `none` to have it show no page at all — signing in then fails without a session there — or another value the provider knows. The provider decides when left out.
- `scopes` (Set of String) Scopes PBS asks the identity provider for, besides `openid`, which it always asks for. Defaults to `["email", "profile"]`, which have the identity provider include the email address and names PBS gives a user it creates. Each is letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, not starting with `.` or `-`.
- `username_claim` (String) Claim whose value is the user name, `<value>@<realm>`, such as `preferred_username`; when left out `sub`, the subject, the only claim the OpenID specification guarantees to be unique. Choose one users cannot change themselves. PBS takes it only when it creates the realm, so changing it replaces the realm.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same value as `realm`, present because Terraform requires an `id`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_realm_openid.authentik
  identity = {
    realm = "authentik"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `realm` (String) Realm name, such as `authentik`.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_realm_openid.authentik
  id = "authentik"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# OpenID realms are imported by name. An import reads no client key: with
# client_key in the configuration, or client_key_wo and its version, the next
# apply sends the configured key to PBS; with neither, PBS keeps its key, until
# a new realm or username_claim replaces the realm without it.
terraform import pbs_realm_openid.authentik authentik
```
